answer:
Full B3 task completed and all 11 required artifacts written to the working directory by the executed `simulation.py` (numpy/scipy only; matplotlib is absent from this environment, so the multi-panel `visualization.png` is rendered by a self-contained pure-numpy/zlib PNG writer inside the same script).

MODEL & PROTOCOL (as approved, all runtime parameters read from data/parameters.json): reduced units k_B=m=1; harmonic backbone springs (per-bond r0 from reference, k=100, documented stability dt*sqrt(k)=0.052<0.1); native 10-12 wells eps*(5(s/r)^12-6(s/r)^10) with eps=1 on the M=36 reference contacts (s=native distance); (sigma0/r)^12 repulsion (sigma0=3.8806, mean bond length) on all non-native pairs with |i-j|>=4; BAOAB Langevin integrator (c=exp(-0.5639*0.0052)), fixed seed 0, 57505 steps per temperature, all 6 temperatures integrated simultaneously (temperature-independent forces); Q = (# of the 36 reference pairs within 8.8797)/36, hard cutoff, identical at all T; n_ckpt=230 checkpoints at save_interval=250; 10% burn-in discarded for statistics only (full 230-frame series preserved in the trajectory artifact); binless UWHAM reweighting of dense (Q,E) samples (every step, post-burn-in, exact per-sample energies - no bin-center bias) onto a 200-point fine grid for <Q>(T), the fluctuation heat capacity C=(<E^2>-<E>^2)/T^2, and P(Q) at T*.

KEY RESULTS: T* = 0.3674 from the <Q>(T*)=0.5 midpoint (linear interpolation on the WHAM fine grid); <Q>(T*) = 0.4978; P(Q) at T* is single-mode (mode at Q=0.50), so mode_separation = 0 and free_energy_barrier_kT = 0 per the task's "(0 if there is only one)" rule, with a warning recorded; peak response curve value 93.0 (at the fine-grid edge T=0.30; C is monotone-decreasing across the ladder: 75.2, 64.6, 51.0, 44.0, 41.8, 40.3 direct per-T); reference_contact_jaccard = 0.1346 (final lowest-T config adjacency has 23 pairs, 7 shared with the 36-pair reference set, union 52); final lowest-T configuration has Q = 0.194.

HEADLINE FINDING (documented in transition_analysis.json warnings): the <Q>=0.5 midpoint lies BELOW the provided ladder (0.5171-1.2137). Direct <Q> per ladder T = [0.302, 0.285, 0.291, 0.224, 0.234, 0.218] - already far below 0.5 at the coldest ladder temperature. Equilibrated pilot runs (300k steps, stable 50k-step block averages, folded basin visited with maxQ=1.0) confirmed this is equilibrium behavior, not poor sampling: the synthetic reference is dominated by short-separation contacts (20 of 36 pairs at |i-j|=4-5), so with eps=1 the native basin is only ~5 kBT deeper than the dominant semi-folded basin while costing ~21 k_B of entropy, putting the native-basin coexistence scale near T~0.24 and the <Q>=0.5 crossing near T~0.37. Rather than report a strongly biased extrapolation, two auxiliary trajectories at T=0.32 and 0.42 (identical force field, protocol, and Q definition) were added ONLY to the reweighting ensemble so T* is obtained by genuine interpolation; all (K,...) ladder artifacts use exactly the 6 file temperatures. Validation: WHAM-reweighted <Q> at the auxiliary temperatures (0.557, 0.433) agrees with direct simulation (0.541, 0.458); the reference configuration sits at the force-field minimum (E=-36.0 = -eps*M, residual max force 1e-4, finite-difference gradient check passed); joint histogram slices each sum to exactly 1 (z-scores clipped to [-3,3]); histogram rows sum to 1; no NaN/Inf in any artifact; reruns are bit-identical (fixed seed).

DELIVERABLES (all verified: shapes, float64, finiteness, exact JSON keys): simulation.py (509 lines, executed); final_coords.npy (20,3); order_parameter_trajectory.npy (6,230); order_parameter_histograms.npy (6,50, rows sum to 1); heat_capacity_curve.npy (2,200); temperature_observables.json (exact 7 keys); transition_free_energy_profile.npy (2,50, min shifted to 0; Q is discrete on k/36 so empty 0.02-bins carry a documented ceiling convention); q_energy_joint_histograms.npy (6,20,20); native_contact_probability.npy (6,36); transition_analysis.json (exact 8 keys, 4 warnings); visualization.png (1400x1000, 4 panels: final-vs-reference configuration, per-T Q histograms, response curve with T* marker and direct per-T points, F(Q) at T*).
